_why: The words the transcription worker writes into scores.transcription_stage,
and where the app puts the bar for each. They are the contract between
mobile/src/lib/transcriptionProgress.ts, and they had drifted twice: the
worker said 'Checking the bar counts' while the app keyed on 'Checking the
reading', and the app held a position for 'Finding the staves' that nothing
had emitted since the Audiveris engine was removed. An unrecognised stage
threw the bar from 70% back to 5% in the middle of a working read.
backend/app/tests/test_stage_parity.py holds the server to this file;
_per_stave_why: A page is read one stave at a time, so the reading step has real measured
progress inside it — the worker knows it has finished 3 of 7. There is no
static key for that: the count is in the words, and the app places them by
interpolating across _reading_band. 'Reading the notation' sits at the top
of that band, not below it, so a split page that falls back to being read
whole does not walk the bar backwards.
_per_page_why: A scan is every page of one part, and the pages are read one after
another. Before this existed a multi-page read reported 'Reading the
notation' for the whole of it — true throughout, and a bar that did
not move once from the first page to the last. The worker's own
comment called that 'a limitation rather than a design' and said the
honest fix was a page counter in the words, waiting on the UI gate.
The count is pages *finished*, so 'Reading page 2 of 3' places the bar
at 1/3 of the reading band: page 1 is done and page 2 has not started.
It never overstates, and it is measured rather than timed.
Per-stave counts are suppressed on a multi-page scan, so the two
counters never fight over the bar: page 2 starting again at 'Reading
stave 1 of 9' would walk it backwards, which is the failure
_whole_page_why: A page read whole reports the provider's name, which is deliberately never
shown: it tells a musician nothing they can act on and quite a lot they did
not ask about. Both forms collapse to the same words.
